question: What do the wise call renunciation of desired actions?
premises: The wise know renunciation of desired actions as complete renunciation.
The discerning call renunciation of all action-fruits renunciation.
Desired rites such as agniṣṭoma are all actions.
For all nitya and naimittika actions, even while being performed, renunciation of the fruit is renunciation.
What remains to be spoken in this chapter was expanded and examined by ancients such as Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara.
For those whose essence is fulfilling the promise of merely clarifying hidden meaning, what is the effort of showing repetition?
Here, for determining the distinction, opinions are presented.
inference: Renunciation is defined as renunciation of action-fruits, and the remaining distinctions are presented here rather than merely repeated.
uncertainties: The supplied glosses are fused and abbreviated, so exact syntactic grouping of several compounds remains uncertain.
The final token “matānyupanyasyati-” appears truncated by a trailing dash.
plain_english: The blessed Lord said: the wise know renunciation of desired actions as complete renunciation; the discerning call renunciation of all action-fruits renunciation. Desired rites such as agniṣṭoma are all actions; for all nitya and naimittika actions, even while being performed, renunciation of the fruit is renunciation. What remains to be spoken in this chapter was expanded and examined by ancients such as Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara; for those whose essence is fulfilling the promise of merely clarifying hidden meaning, what is the effort of showing repetition? Here, for determining the distinction, opinions are presented.
